headline: This law changes the rules for forgiving COVID-19 Paycheck Protection Program loans that small businesses received, giving them more time and flexibility.
what_it_does: The law changes how forgivable Paycheck Protection Program loans work for small businesses. It lets borrowers spend loan money over a longer period and still qualify for forgiveness, and it raises the share of a loan that can go to non-payroll costs like rent and utilities from 25% to 40%. It also gives employers more time to rehire workers or restore pay levels without losing forgiveness, and sets new repayment rules for loans that are not forgiven, including a five-year minimum term for any remaining balance.

who_it_affects.group: Small businesses that received Paycheck Protection Program loans
who_it_affects.how: They can spend more of their loan on non-payroll costs, have more time to rehire workers or restore wages, and may qualify for more forgiveness.

who_it_affects.group: Small businesses that have not yet applied for loan forgiveness
who_it_affects.how: They get a longer window to apply, and if they do not apply, they have 10 months after the program ends to start making loan payments.

who_it_affects.group: Employers who cannot rehire former workers or return to prior business levels due to COVID-19 rules
who_it_affects.how: Their forgivable loan amount is figured without penalty for lower headcount if they cannot rehire similarly qualified workers or restore activity because of federal COVID-19 requirements.

who_it_affects.group: Borrowers whose loans are only partly forgiven
who_it_affects.how: The leftover balance must be repayable over at least five years.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted June 5, 2020; the changes apply to Paycheck Protection Program loans under the program's rules at that time.
